cards.text: Last chapter of Leviticus, friend, and the LORD has more to say to Moses. He tells Moses to speak to the Israelites about this: what happens when someone makes a special vow to the LORD involving the value of persons.

Then comes a whole price list in silver, set by age and by male or female, from one month old all the way to sixty and older. Top of the list is a man from twenty to sixty at fifty shekels, and friend, I came with a price sticker that said 25 CENTS.

cards.question: Now somebody makes that vow, but they're too poor to pay the price on the list. What happens?

answers.text: The priest sets a price they can afford
The vow is canceled at no cost
A neighbor pays the full price for them

cards.text: Next up: animals. Somebody vows an animal that may be brought as an offering to the LORD.

cards.question: An animal fit to be brought as an offering is vowed to the LORD. What does it become?

answers.text: Free to return to the herd

cards.question: Once an offering animal is vowed to the LORD, the owner may swap it for a better one.
The owner swaps his vowed animal for another one anyway. Which animal ends up holy?

cards.text: He tried to trade one animal and ended up giving TWO. That's not a swap, friend, that's a two-for-one sale and HE'S the one paying.
Now, what if the vow involves an unclean animal, one that may not be brought as an offering to the LORD? That one gets handled differently.

cards.question: When an unclean animal is vowed, the ___ sets its value, whether high or low.
The owner decides he wants to buy back the unclean animal he vowed. What must he do?

answers.text: Add a fifth to its value

cards.text: Now a man consecrates his whole HOUSE as holy to the LORD, and the priest values it, good or bad. Friend, I spent years in a junk drawer, so a whole house sounds like a castle to me.

cards.question: If the man wants his consecrated house back, he can redeem it by paying the assessed value plus a fifth.

cards.text: Now land: a man consecrates a parcel of his land to the LORD, and it's valued by the seed it takes, fifty shekels of silver for every homer of barley seed. If he does it during the Year of Jubilee, that price stands.

cards.question: But say the man consecrates his field after the Jubilee. How does the priest figure the price?

answers.text: By the years left until the next Jubilee
By how big last year's harvest was
By what the owner first paid for it

cards.question: If the man who consecrated the field wants it back, he can redeem it by adding a fifth to its value.
Now say the man never buys his consecrated field back, or he sells it to another man. Can it be redeemed after that?

answers.text: No it can no longer be redeemed
Yes by adding a fifth to its value
Yes once the Year of Jubilee comes

cards.question: When that field is released in the Jubilee, it becomes holy and belongs to the priests.

cards.text: Now a man consecrates a field he bought, one that isn't part of his own property. The priest figures its value up to the Year of Jubilee, and the man pays it that same day as a sacred offering to the LORD.

cards.question: A man consecrated a field he bought. When the Year of Jubilee comes, where does that field go?

cards.text: Every value uses the sanctuary shekel, twenty gerahs to the shekel, so it's the same measuring cup for everybody. Then comes a firstborn of the livestock, an ox or a sheep, and nobody may consecrate one.

cards.question: Why can't anyone consecrate a firstborn ox or sheep to the LORD?

answers.text: It already belongs to the LORD
It is too young to be offered
It belongs to the oldest son

cards.text: You can't give somebody what's already theirs, friend. That's like a baker gift-wrapping MY oven and yelling, "Surprise, Papa!"

cards.question: A firstborn that's an unclean animal can be redeemed with a fifth added. If it isn't redeemed, it is ___ according to its value.

cards.text: Now a different word: devoted. A man sets apart something he owns to the LORD, whether a man, an animal or his inherited land, and everything so devoted is most holy to the LORD.

cards.question: A man can buy back something he devoted to the LORD by adding a fifth to its value.

cards.text: And no person set apart for destruction may be ransomed. He must surely be put to death.
Last topic, friend: the tithe from the land, whether it comes from the seed of the land or the fruit of the trees.

cards.question: The tithe from the land's seed and fruit trees is holy. Who does it belong to?

cards.text: Want to buy back part of your tithe? Add a fifth, and friend, by now you could TEACH this class.

cards.question: Every ___ animal from the herd or flock that passes under the shepherd's rod is holy to the LORD.
While counting the herd, the owner may check whether each tenth animal is good or bad and swap it out.

cards.text: No inspecting, no swapping, and if he swaps anyway, both animals are holy and neither can be redeemed. These are the commandments the LORD gave Moses for the Israelites on Mount Sinai, and friend, you just baked through ALL of Leviticus!
